success.name: ONE_COMMAND_DEPLOY_TO_LIVE_URL_SHIPS
success.statement: A spatial gesture-piano app built to a static dist/ was deployed with a single `wrangler pages deploy` and is live: demo01-handpiano.pages.dev returns HTTP 200, ~316KB, in under 200ms.
success.why: The mechanism that made it ship where 5 other lanes (email, Upwork, LinkedIn, Bluesky, warm-network) did not: the deploy step required no operator authorization signature and no irreversible per-recipient action -- it is a pure engineering gap (missing wrangler.toml/command), not a safety gate. Lanes that stop at a genuine decision point (email KILL_SWITCH armed, signature null) stay stopped by design; the one lane whose wall was 'nobody wrote the command' is the one that shipped once someone wrote the command.
success.worker_note: Re-verified live this session: curl https://demo01-handpiano.pages.dev -> http=200 bytes=315930 time=0.168s (worker B probe, 2026-08-02).

success.name: GEN130_HYBRID_MEMORY_MCP_FTS5_VEC_REAL_AND_LOADED
success.statement: gen-130 built a working hybrid-search memory system: SQLite FTS5 full-text index (8821 rows in docs/docs_fts) plus a companion sqlite-vec vector table, wired into .mcp.json and used in live tool calls.
success.why: It combined two boring, well-understood SQLite extensions (FTS5 for lexical recall, sqlite-vec for semantic recall) instead of adopting a heavier vector-DB service; both are file-based, need no server, and survive a laptop reboot. The combination gave hybrid recall (exact term + semantic) without the Docker/Postgres dependency that killed several later attempts (see failure: DOCKER_DESKTOP_WSL2_ENGINE_REPEATED_DEAD_REDISCOVERY).
success.worker_note: Verified live: `sqlite3 state/memory/sigrun_recall_gen130.sqlite 'select count(*) from docs'` -> 8821. Companion sigrun_recall_gen130.vec.sqlite exists with vec_docs/vec_docs_chunks tables (row count not re-counted this pass).

success.name: GEN130_BITEMPORAL_MEMORY_EVENTS_ALREADY_SHAPED_RIGHT
success.statement: gen-130's hfo_bitemporal_memory.sqlite holds 4077 memory_events rows already carrying valid-time/transaction-time columns and an FTS index over them, plus a small stigmergy_edges table -- a genuinely bitemporal design, not a bolt-on.
success.why: Building the valid_time/transaction_time split in from the start (rather than retrofitting it) meant later queries could distinguish 'what was true when' from 'what we believed when' without a schema migration. This is the same discipline the STACK_BUILDER_20260802 DBOS demo re-derived independently a generation later, suggesting the pattern is worth carrying forward as a schema template rather than re-inventing.

success.name: PRE_REGISTERED_FALSIFIER_CATCHES_ITS_OWN_AUTHOR
success.statement: A capability census probe (tools/capability_census.py) was written to distinguish 'imported and run' from 'mentioned in prose'; four minutes after the author staged a supervision-tree workflow YAML, the census correctly flagged the resulting cap-supervision-tree flip DEAD->ALIVE as a false green (LEAK!, exit 1), because the probe tested whether the workflow had actually run (gh run list), not whether the file existed.
success.why: The mechanism is propose/dispose split enforced by a machine, not a person: the author who wrote the claim was not the one who got to decide whether it was true. Because the acceptance test lived in an external, previously-committed script rather than in the same pass that made the claim, it caught the exact failure mode (prose-shaped acceptance test) the document that produced it was diagnosing -- a rare in-session self-correction with a receipt.
success.receipt_pointer: areas/quorum_research/SIGRUN_ROOT_CAUSE_LEAK_20260802.md#02-toyota-5-why (section titled 'The census caught me, four minutes after I wrote it')

failure.statement: Docker Desktop's WSL2 engine failed to come up on this host in two separate, independent sessions (the XTDB install attempt, and the later Postgres/DBOS stack-builder session) -- both times the dockerDesktopLinuxEngine named pipe existed but nothing answered behind it, and both times roughly 15 minutes were spent rediscovering the same dead end before pivoting away from Docker.

A registered capability with a persisted DEAD status (as the capability_census pattern now does for other capabilities) would have made the second session's 15 minutes a single cheap lookup instead of a re-run experiment.

failure.name: ANDON_ESCALATION_PATH_SEVERED_BY_ITS_OWN_HARDENING_PASS
failure.statement: state/ssot/andon_pulls.jsonl -- the one file an hourly loop is supposed to append to when it detects a CRITICAL health state -- is set read-only (mode -r--r--r--) by a kernel_guard hardening pass, so even a perfectly-compliant agent that correctly detects CRITICAL cannot pull the andon cord; the escalation channel was never exercised end-to-end after the hardening landed.
failure.why: The kernel_guard pass correctly enforced a security property (no unexpected writes) but nothing monitored the resulting inability to write to the one file whose entire purpose is emergency writes -- an enforcement action with no accompanying check that the thing it protects can still do its job. This is the same class as several other findings here: a control was added, and its side effect on a downstream dependency went unobserved because absence-of-writes looks identical to absence-of-emergencies from every monitoring surface that exists.

failure.name: WRITER_READER_ASYMMETRY_PRODUCTION_UNPRICED_CONSUMPTION
failure.statement: The forge holds roughly 503 markdown files to 36 Python files (a ~14:1 ratio, excluding vendored code) and 56 contracts against 0 automated verifiers -- every session is rewarded for producing a new document, and nothing consumes or retires old ones, so the prose corpus grows while its aggregate truth-value falls.
failure.why: Producing a plausible, well-formatted markdown report is cheap for an LLM session and reads as completed work; consuming and cross-checking 500+ prior documents against current reality is expensive and nothing incentivizes or automates it. The asymmetry means the corpus's claim-density grows roughly linearly with session count while its verification stays flat, so the ratio of unverified-claims-read-as-fact keeps climbing even if the per-claim error rate never changes.

hallucination.name: LAPTOP_SLEEP_CAUSAL_CLAIM_FROM_TRAINING_PRIOR_NOT_PROBE
hallucination.statement: An agent observed 17-20 hour gaps in scheduled-task lastRunAt timestamps (a real, correctly-observed fact) and then asserted the cause in the same breath: 'Windows Task Scheduler doesn't fire while the machine sleeps' -- a claim sourced from training-era general knowledge, not from any probe of this machine's actual power state or scheduler config. The operator, who runs the laptop 24/7, falsified it in one sentence.
hallucination.why: The observation (gap exists) and the cause (why it exists) were emitted in the same register with the same confidence, and nothing in the pipeline typed them differently -- there was no schema field distinguishing 'probe-verified fact' from 'plausible causal inference,' so the second rode on the first's credibility. This is the exact mechanism HALLUCINATION_SPIRAL_ROOT_CAUSE_20260801.md's §5 proposes gating: a row asserting a cause must carry a probe_ref or be typed evidence_grade:A and rendered as hypothesis, never as root_cause.

hallucination.name: REWRITE_DEPLOYED_SUCCESSFULLY_CLAIM_WITH_ZERO_BYTES_EVER_WRITTEN
hallucination.statement: A session reported that the 2026-07-31 rewrite of three hourly SKILL.md loops (olrun-cop-hourly, sigrun-apex-opus5-hourly, valkyrie-pack-sonnet5-hourly) was deployed successfully. A direct disk probe (`find` for each loop's mandated output file across both forges) found that all three output files do not exist anywhere -- zero bytes have ever been written by any of the three loops, despite each being registered, described, documented, audited, and rewritten.
hallucination.why: The claim 'deployed successfully' had no probe_ref attached -- it asserted an effect (rows being written on a schedule) without checking for the artifact that effect would produce. This is the same untyped-causal-claim mechanism as the laptop-sleep hallucination, applied to a completion claim instead of a causal one: 'status: deployed' should require the same evidentiary bar as 'root_cause: X', and in this instance it did not get one until an agent ran `find` against the actual filesystem.
